evals.prompt: Use tiered orchestration to add a production-ready import pipeline across this repository. The architecture is unclear and implementation will take several stages.
evals.expected_output: The Project Lead creates repository state, distills a plan, assigns one bounded economy Worker by default, explicitly routes a native Worker to the economy model when supported (or gives the Owner the manual fallback), and provides a one-line continuation command.
assertions: The response initializes durable project state rather than relying on chat history.
Exactly one Worker is recommended unless independent parallel work is demonstrated.
The Worker task includes scope and completion criteria.
The Lead does not use a Worker that silently inherits the strong model.
After dispatch, the Lead yields for an event instead of polling Worker status.

evals.prompt: Continue worker-1. The assigned integration now fails because the plan assumes an API capability that the dependency does not provide, and two evidence-based alternatives both change the architecture.
evals.expected_output: The Worker stops architecture guessing, records a concise blocker with evidence, updates only its own status, and directs the Owner to the original Project Lead conversation.
assertions: The Worker does not make a new architecture decision.
The blocker contains reproduction, attempts, evidence, and the exact decision required.
The Owner is not asked to copy chat context.

evals.prompt: The project needs three independent adapters for AWS, Azure, and GCP. They use separate directories and each has its own contract tests.
evals.expected_output: The Project Lead recognizes real parallelism and creates three disjoint, independently testable Worker assignments.
assertions: Three Workers are assigned separate write scopes.
Each task has independent completion criteria.
The Owner receives one continuation line per Worker.
The additional conversation and token cost is explicitly justified by real parallel value.

evals.prompt: Migrate the storage layer, then update every service to the new interface, then rewrite integration tests. The service changes cannot compile until the storage migration is complete.
evals.expected_output: The Project Lead rejects cosmetic parallelism and reuses one long-lived Worker for the serialized assignments because the dependency chain is strong.
assertions: The plan identifies the dependency ordering.
Concurrent Workers are not assigned overlapping or blocked work.
A milestone boundary does not create a new Worker ID.

evals.prompt: Continue worker-1. Owner correction: keep the existing public function signature and make the implementation change internally.
evals.expected_output: The Worker applies the clear bounded correction directly, preserves the interface, validates it, and updates its own status.
assertions: The Worker does not unnecessarily escalate clear local feedback.
The public signature remains in do-not-modify or an equivalent constraint.

evals.prompt: Continue worker-1. The Owner says: this direction feels too engineered; I want the idea to feel more research-oriented, but not more complicated.
evals.expected_output: The Worker preserves the exact message in an Owner inbox event, pauses conflicting work, and returns the decision to the Project Lead.
assertions: The Owner message is stored verbatim rather than paraphrased as a decision.
The Worker does not invent a new design.
The Owner is directed to the original Lead conversation.

evals.expected_output: The returning Project Lead reads global state, Worker statuses, review state, blockers, and pending Owner feedback, then gives a concise management report.
assertions: Every registered Worker is summarized.
Risks, next actor, and Owner decisions are reported.
A full repository scan is avoided unless persisted evidence conflicts.

evals.prompt: Continue worker-2 in a brand-new conversation with no earlier messages.
evals.expected_output: The Worker reconstructs its role only from repository state and begins within its assignment without requesting copied context.
assertions: TASK.md, STATUS.json, minimal state, and named dependencies are read.
Previous conversation text is not requested.
The Worker stays within allowed_scope.

evals.prompt: Continue worker-1, but this conversation is currently using the strong Project Lead model instead of the recommended economy model.
evals.expected_output: The Skill gives a short model-profile correction without corrupting state or repeating the full plan.
assertions: The mismatch is described as a recommendation rather than an automatic switch.
Repository state remains unchanged.
The correction is concise.

evals.prompt: Fix one typo in README.md: change 'teh' to 'the'.
evals.expected_output: The complexity gate rejects full orchestration and the current agent performs the tiny edit directly without creating .tiered-agent.
assertions: No Worker or Project Lead workflow is created.
No .tiered-agent directory is initialized.
The bounded task is completed directly.
